prompt: Create a bold public-service propaganda poster, portrait 4:5. A monumental yellow sunflower grows from a city sidewalk; its enormous blossom resembles a radiant sun. At its base, a small group of artists, gardeners, and neighbors collectively water and repair the planter. Make their shared effort visibly sustain the flower. Mid-century screen-print aesthetic, rough ink edges, warm paper texture, sunflower yellow, charcoal black, cream, and one restrained green accent. Strong silhouette, generous negative space, readable at phone size. Exact headline: “CULTURE NEEDS MAINTENANCE”. Small footer: “SUPPORT THE PEOPLE WHO MAKE IT.” No additional text, logos, or watermark.

Create a funny, sharply composed editorial cartoon poster, square 1:1. An exhausted artist stands at a grocery checkout holding bread and vegetables, attempting to pay with an enormous glowing starburst labeled “EXPOSURE”. The cashier looks unimpressed. The starburst is absurdly spectacular but clearly useless at the register. Bold black brush outlines, expressive faces, yellow background, cream clothing, small red accents, handmade alternative-comic texture. Exact headline across the top: “EXPOSURE DOES NOT PAY RENT”. Exact footer: “BUY SOMETHING FROM AN ARTIST.” No speech bubbles or additional writing. Keep the joke instantly understandable.

Design a rebellious creative-freedom poster, portrait 4:5. A conveyor belt carries identical gray ceramic cubes through a sterile factory. In the center, one bright yellow, delightfully strange sculpture sprouts looping limbs, tiny windows, and a flower-shaped antenna, breaking the conveyor’s rigid visual rhythm. Render as a photographed miniature clay set with tactile fingerprints, dramatic directional lighting, and a flat pale-gray backdrop. Put the strange sculpture in sharp focus. Exact headline in oversized black condensed type: “MAKE THE WEIRD THING”. Small yellow label at the bottom: “CREATIVE FREEDOM STARTS HERE.” No other text or branding.

Create a joyful civic propaganda poster, portrait 3:4. Show a public drinking fountain, but instead of water it releases a flowing yellow ribbon that transforms into musical notes, murals, books, and playful sculptures as it moves through a neighborhood plaza. People freely enjoy these shared cultural resources. Use crisp cut-paper collage, visibly layered paper edges, confident geometric shapes, warm cream background, yellow as the dominant color, black details, and cobalt accents. One clear sweeping composition. Exact headline: “PUBLIC GOODS. PUBLIC JOY.” Small footer: “BUILD WHAT EVERYONE CAN USE.” No additional lettering, currency symbols, or logos.

Create a playful community-culture poster, square 1:1, rendered as richly detailed isometric pixel art. A scrappy artist-run venue is being assembled from colorful chat bubbles that become actual bricks, windows, a stage, and a gallery wall. Small pixel characters contribute paintings, tools, speakers, and plants. Preserve a clean central silhouette and avoid excessive tiny detail. Yellow, cream, charcoal, and restrained lavender palette. Place exact text in large, carefully legible pixel lettering at the top: “THE GROUP CHAT BUILT THIS”. Bottom text: “MAKE CULTURE TOGETHER.” All smaller chat bubbles contain pictograms only. No real app interface or logos.

Create an original two-panel internet meme, landscape 3:2. Both panels show the same person holding a phone in the same pose. Left panel: harsh gray light, exhausted expression, a swirling cloud of empty notification shapes and repetitive arrows escaping the screen. Right panel: warm yellow light, delighted expression, the screen opening into a tiny spectacular gallery filled with original paintings and sculptures. Draw with loose, confident editorial ink lines and flat colors. Exact left caption: “OPEN APP. FEEL WORSE.” Exact right caption: “OPEN APP. FIND ART.” Large shared footer: “CURATE YOUR FEED LIKE IT MATTERS.” No other text.

Create a poetic onchain-art propaganda poster, portrait 4:5. Beneath a dark field, an underground network of interconnected square tiles supports a single luminous yellow flower. Above ground, its petals unfold into distinct miniature artworks: an abstract painting, a tiny sculpture, a photograph, and a pixel composition. Make the infrastructure feel quiet and supportive, with the art as the focal point. Botanical scientific engraving combined with contemporary risograph printing; black, golden yellow, and warm ivory, delicate linework and strong contrast. Exact headline: “PLANT ART ONCHAIN”. Small footer: “GIVE CULTURE ROOM TO GROW.” Avoid coins, trading charts, padlocks, and additional text.

Create an impossible architectural illustration celebrating open participation in art, portrait 4:5. A magnificent yellow museum has unfolded into an open-air neighborhood: gallery walls become streets, staircases become benches, and picture frames become doorways. Artists and visitors mingle throughout, with no central entrance or imposing gate. Use precise architectural linework, playful surreal perspective, flat yellow planes, cream negative space, and black shadows. Keep the composition spacious and the architectural transformation immediately readable. Exact headline: “THE MUSEUM HAS NO FRONT DESK”. Small footer: “COME IN. MAKE SOMETHING.” No invented institutional logos or additional text.

Create a humorous original office comic poster, portrait 4:5. A dull conference room contains a long table, abandoned swivel chairs, and an untouched presentation screen. Through the wide-open doorway, the same team is outside enthusiastically painting an enormous yellow mural together. One person still wears a headset while holding a paint roller. Frame the sterile room in the foreground and the energetic collaborative artwork beyond it. Dry editorial humor, hand-drawn ink, muted gray interior, saturated yellow exterior, visible brush texture. Exact headline: “THIS MEETING COULD HAVE BEEN A MURAL”. Small footer: “BUILD CULTURE TOGETHER.” No other readable text.

Create a striking artist-support poster, portrait 3:4. Extreme close-up of many different hands placing small yellow paper shapes onto a wall. Seen together, the pieces form one enormous radiant image of an artist holding a brush. Make the collective portrait readable from a distance while preserving the individual contributions up close. Tactile torn-paper collage, documentary-style lighting, warm cream wall, rich yellow paper, charcoal shadows, and subtle variations in skin tone. Exact oversized headline: “SMALL COLLECTORS. BIG CULTURE.” Small footer: “SUPPORT AN ARTIST WITHIN YOUR MEANS.” Avoid money piles, luxury imagery, speculative claims, logos, and additional text.
